title: Hapag-Lloyd lifts Asia-Europe rates to $6,800
metaDescription: Hapag-Lloyd's 1 December FAK rise, CMA CGM's $650 Africa surcharge, and a Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen that could move your tariff bill.
bottomLine: Hapag-Lloyd will charge up to $6,800 per 40-foot box from the Far East to Europe from 1 December, a rise you can still beat by booking before the cut-off. CMA CGM adds $650 per TEU to South Africa in the same window. Trump and Xi meet in Shenzhen on Thursday with a $60bn tariff package still unsigned, so do not price your Q1 on a deal that has not landed.

stories.headline: Hapag-Lloyd lifts Far East to Europe FAK to $6,800 per 40ft from 1 December
stories.tldr: Hapag-Lloyd will charge up to $6,800 per 40-foot container from the Far East to Europe from 1 December 2026.
stories.whatHappened:
Hapag-Lloyd has published revised Freight All Kinds ocean tariff rates for shipments from the Far East to Europe, effective 1 December 2026. The highest published rate reaches US$6,800 per 40-foot container.

The new tariffs apply to 20-foot and 40-foot dry containers, including high-cube equipment, on sailings with a date of loading from 1 December. FAK rates are the published tariff a carrier will quote for general cargo without a named shipper contract. The announcement covers the Far East to Europe trade only.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you ship general cargo from China to Rotterdam, Hamburg or Felixstowe on FAK terms, your per-unit ocean cost jumps on any container loaded from 1 December. A 40-foot high-cube at $6,800 is the ceiling in the published table, and high-cube is what most furniture, flat-pack and oversize ecommerce sellers actually book. Work out your landed cost on the new number before you quote a retail price for Q1.

This hits sellers running low-margin, bulky goods hardest. If your box carries 800 units at $8 landed, a $1,000 rate move is $1.25 a unit. If it carries 200 units of furniture, it is $5 a unit and your margin is gone. Anyone with a signed service contract is insulated until that contract expires, so check your expiry date this week.

The practical lever is the cut-off. Cargo loaded before 1 December sails on the old tariff. You have roughly two weeks of booking window, and the pre-December sailings will fill as other sellers read the same notice.
stories.hotTake: Carriers publish these rises to anchor the negotiation, not to collect them. The $6,800 is a ceiling, and the real number your forwarder gets will be lower if you commit volume. I would not panic-book a container I do not need. I would call my forwarder on Monday, ask what they can hold for December loading, and get it in writing before space tightens.
actions: Check your service contract expiry date and confirm in writing whether December loadings sit on contract or FAK rates.
Ask your forwarder to quote the 1 December FAK level on your actual box size before you reprice any Q1 listing.

stories.headline: CMA CGM adds $650 per TEU peak season surcharge on Far East to South Africa
stories.tldr: CMA CGM will add a $650 per TEU peak season surcharge on Far East to South Africa shipments in November and December 2026.
stories.whatHappened:
CMA CGM has announced new Peak Season Surcharges covering shipments from the Far East to South Africa and from Europe and the Mediterranean to Latin America and the Caribbean. Implementation dates fall in November and December 2026.

The carrier will introduce a surcharge of US$650 per TEU on shipments from the Far East. The full text was not available, so the precise start date and the scope of the Latin America and Caribbean surcharge are not published in the summary.

A PSS sits on top of the base ocean freight rate. It is charged per container, not per kilogram, so it lands hardest on light, bulky cargo where the base rate is already spread thin.
stories.whyItMatters:
South Africa is a real lane for Chinese sellers now, particularly in homeware, solar accessories, small appliances and phone accessories, where Takealot and independent Shopify stores have grown fast. A $650 per TEU surcharge on a 20-foot box is roughly $0.65 a unit if you load 1,000 units, and $6.50 a unit if you load 100. Know which one you are.

The surcharge is per TEU, so if you ship 40-foot boxes you will pay it on a two-TEU basis unless the carrier applies it differently. Confirm the basis in writing with your forwarder, because the announcement does not spell it out.

If you sell into South Africa and your Q4 stock is already on the water, this does not touch you. If you are booking December production for a January arrival, it does, and you should decide now whether to absorb it or move the price.
stories.hotTake: Peak season surcharges on secondary lanes are where carriers make their margin, because nobody negotiates them. Sellers fight over Asia-Europe and Asia-US and then accept whatever lands on Africa. I would treat the $650 as a floor and ask my forwarder for a named-account exemption. Half the time you get one, and the other half you learn your forwarder is not trying.
actions: Confirm with your forwarder whether the $650 applies per TEU on 40-foot bookings and the exact first sailing date it bites.
Recalculate landed cost on your South Africa SKUs and decide now whether to absorb the surcharge or move retail pricing.

stories.headline: Trump and Xi meet in Shenzhen on Thursday with $60bn tariff package unsigned
stories.tldr: Trump and Xi meet in Shenzhen on Thursday with a proposed $60bn reciprocal tariff cut package still unfinished.
stories.whatHappened:
Chinese and US officials held their first trade council meeting on Friday, discussing tariff reductions and agricultural trade. China's Commerce Ministry said Saturday that talks covered reciprocal tariff reductions and agricultural purchases.

The negotiations included a proposed arrangement under which each country would implement approximately $30 billion in tariff cuts, part of a broader $60 billion package first proposed at a September summit in Washington. Beijing described the discussions as constructive but did not say whether new agreements were reached.

Trump and Xi are scheduled to meet Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen. Agricultural trade remains an obstacle: Chinese purchases of US farm products excluding soybeans are heading toward their lowest annual level in seven years.
stories.whyItMatters:
A $30 billion US tariff cut, if it lands, changes your cost per unit on US-bound goods. It does not land on Thursday. It lands after a signed agreement, a Federal Register notice and a customs implementation date, which is weeks or months away. Do not price your Q1 US listings on a deal that has not been signed.

The meeting matters for a different reason. If it goes badly, expect the export control and enforcement rhetoric to harden, and expect CBP scrutiny on Chinese-origin goods to tighten. That shows up as longer dwell times and more requests for documentation, not as a headline rate change.

For UK and EU sellers, the direct tariff effect is small. The indirect effect is on your supplier's confidence and on factory lead times if US buyers pull orders forward on deal optimism. Watch whether your factory quotes firm or vague delivery dates next week.
stories.hotTake: Every seller I know has been waiting for this deal since September and has lost two months of planning to it. The package is $60bn across two economies, which is rounding error against total trade, and agriculture is still blocking it. Plan on current tariff rates through Q1 and treat any cut as upside. You will sleep better and you will quote faster.
actions: Price Q1 US-bound listings on current tariff rates and treat any reduction as margin you did not plan for.
Ask your main supplier whether US buyers are pulling orders forward and whether that is stretching your lead times.

stories.headline: Shenzhen hosts 115 Fortune Global 500 firms at Apec CEO Summit this week
stories.tldr: Shenzhen expects representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies at the Apec CEO Summit, its largest multilateral event.
stories.whatHappened:
Shenzhen expects more than 100 major global enterprises and over a dozen national leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit. Li Qingshuang, vice-chairperson of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, gave the figure at a press conference on Sunday.

Representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies will participate, Li said. The event is the highest-level multilateral gathering Shenzhen has hosted.

The Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting runs from 18 to 19 November in the city. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to meet alongside it.
stories.whyItMatters:
Shenzhen is where a large share of your suppliers, your inspection agents and your forwarders sit. A week of road closures, hotel sellouts and security cordons around Futian and the convention district will slow factory visits, sample pickups and warehouse collections.

If you have a sourcing trip booked for this week, expect your meetings to run late and your drivers to be rerouted. If you have a container scheduled to load out of Yantian or Shekou, check with your forwarder whether trucking has been given restricted windows. Port operations usually continue, but the drayage between factory and terminal is where the delay shows up.

Book your QC inspections and factory audits for the following week if you can move them. A missed inspection slot in peak season costs you more than a rescheduled flight.
stories.hotTake: Every Apec in China produces a week of gridlock and a stack of signed MOUs that nobody reads. The useful part is that it forces a Trump-Xi meeting, and that meeting is the only thing on the calendar that can move your tariff line this quarter. I would use the week to push suppliers on delivery dates while they are distracted by the attention.
actions: Move any factory visits, QC inspections or sample pickups in Shenzhen to the week of 23 November.
Ask your forwarder whether trucking windows to Yantian or Shekou are restricted during the summit.

contentHooks: Hapag-Lloyd's $6,800 ceiling is an anchor, not a price. The number your forwarder gets is the one that matters.
Two weeks of booking window before 1 December is the only real lever Hapag-Lloyd just handed you.
A $650 per TEU surcharge on South Africa is $6.50 a unit if you ship 100 units and $0.65 if you ship 1,000.
Nobody negotiates peak season surcharges on secondary lanes, which is exactly why carriers put them there.
The $60bn tariff package has been two months away since September. Price Q1 on current rates and stop waiting.
Apec in Shenzhen will not move your freight rate, but it will move your QC inspection slot.
Every seller waiting on the tariff deal has lost two months of planning to a negotiation that agriculture is still blocking.
Check your service contract expiry this week. It is the difference between $6,800 and whatever you signed.
The pre-Chinese New Year rush starts earlier than most sellers plan for, and this year it follows a crowded Q4.
A missed factory inspection during Apec week costs more than a rescheduled flight.

faq.question: When does the Hapag-Lloyd Far East to Europe rate increase take effect?
faq.answer: From 1 December 2026, on sailings with a loading date from that day. The highest published rate reaches US$6,800 per 40-foot container, and the tariffs apply to 20-foot and 40-foot dry containers including high-cube equipment. Cargo loaded before 1 December sails on the old tariff, so you have roughly two weeks of booking window. Confirm whether your booking sits on a service contract or the new FAK rates before you reprice anything.

faq.question: How much is the CMA CGM peak season surcharge on South Africa shipments?
faq.answer: US$650 per TEU on shipments from the Far East to South Africa, with implementation dates in November and December 2026. The announcement does not specify the exact start date or how the charge applies to 40-foot bookings, so get the basis in writing from your forwarder. On a 20-foot box carrying 1,000 units the surcharge is about $0.65 a unit. On 100 units it is $6.50 a unit.

faq.question: Will the Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen cut US tariffs on Chinese goods?
faq.answer: Not immediately. Officials discussed a proposed arrangement under which each country would implement approximately $30 billion in tariff cuts, part of a $60 billion package first proposed in September. Beijing called the talks constructive but announced no new agreements, and agricultural trade remains an obstacle. Even a signed deal needs a Federal Register notice and a customs implementation date. Price Q1 US listings on current rates and treat any cut as upside.

faq.question: Will Apec in Shenzhen delay my shipments this week?
faq.answer: Port operations usually continue, but drayage between factory and terminal is where delays show up. Shenzhen expects representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies and over a dozen national leaders, with the leaders' meeting on 18 and 19 November. Expect road closures and restricted trucking windows around Futian. Ask your forwarder whether Yantian and Shekou collections are affected, and move factory visits to the week of 23 November.
